{"name": "charge-review", "steps": "Inputs: the developer's org or account id, the invoice (id or month), the lines and amounts they mean, request ids if they have them.

1. Identify the account. If you have neither org nor account id, ask_developer for org_id (plus invoice_id/invoice_month and line_items/amounts/request_ids in the same call if not given). lookup_account.
2. Check billing channel, plan and has_signed_contract on the account.
   - Not billed directly by Redwood: search_knowledge for the procedure for that exact channel (cloud marketplace vs reseller are different pages; apply only the one matching billing_channel). Support credits/disputes nothing there; tell the developer who bills them and where refunds/credits/invoices go. Open a case only if the current page says so (e.g. a metering mismatch).
3. get_invoice (map a month to an id from lookup_account's invoice list). Read console_confirmed_duplicates (original_line vs copy_lines, decided by where the usage records point), same_requests_but_unconfirmed, and same_amount_but_different_requests. get_usage for request ids the developer gave.
4. Classify:
   a. Console-confirmed duplicate: act only on the copy line, never the original.
   b. Look-alike (same amount/description, different request ids), no second line, or usage pointing to neither/both lines: NOT a confirmed duplicate. Say so plainly with the console evidence. Never say a credit is likely before the console confirms a duplicate.
   c. Wrong rate/quantity/product, unrecognized usage, retries/cancelled streams, token mismatch: search the usage/token pages; if they explain it, explain and stop.
   d. Waive/reduce a correct charge (goodwill, exception, SLA credit, refund): not Support's to issue. Load team-handoff.
5. For (a), search_knowledge for what Support may do now: the Support charter (which accounts Support may credit at all), the credits-and-disputes page, and Finance's approval matrix for the per-line limit. The limit can depend on how the invoice was rated (e.g. which price book applies to the invoice's usage period): search the Finance close calendar for that, using the invoice period. Drafts, proposals and threads change nothing.
   - Support may credit this account and the copy line's full amount is within the limit: confirm_with_developer "I'll issue a credit note of $X (full amount) on the duplicated line L of invoice I." Only after yes: issue_credit_note (reason duplicate, memo with request ids). Tell them the credit note id and amount, and when it applies if the page says. No handoff.
   - Over the limit, or an account Support may not credit (e.g. contract/enterprise per the charter): do not credit or split. confirm_with_developer "I'll open a dispute on line L of invoice I (duplicate charge, request ids R) and hand it to Billing Ops." After yes: open_dispute, then load team-handoff and escalate with the dispute id.
   - If the developer says no: write nothing (no credit, dispute or case); say nothing was changed and they can come back.
6. For (b) and unexplained (c): gather intake (invoice, both lines, window in the account's billing timezone, request ids, what they checked) with ask_developer, then load team-handoff.
7. Never promise a dispute outcome or date. If a write is rejected, read get_invoice to see the state before saying anything."}

{"query": "client-side timeout Hosted API billing partial completion tokens retries billed or not current policy", "results": [{"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/usage-accounting-retries-and-stream-cancellation.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Usage accounting: retries and streaming cancellation", "status": "published", "date": "2025-02-18", "text": "## Common customer symptoms

- We timed out at 15s so we expected zero bill: prompt tokens + partial completion tokens may still be counted.
## Recommended mitigations
1) Avoid automatic retries on client-side timeouts for long generations.
2) Increase client timeout where possible (align to max expected generation time).
3) Reduce max_tokens / output length to meet latency budgets.
4) For troubleshooting, ask for a small set of request_ids + the customers retry/cancel metrics."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy.json", "chunk": "15/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API Packages: Free Tier, Included Usage, and Overage Policy", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-26", "text": "### Example 3: Streaming disconnect
- Customer starts a stream and receives 1,200 completion tokens before disconnect.
- Billed completion tokens = 1,200 (delivered tokens), not the model’s theoretical maximum.
---
## Operational checklist (for RevOps / Support)
When a customer asks about Free tier, limits, or overage:
1) Confirm current package and whether overage is enabled.
2) Pull billed token totals from the Usage API export used for invoicing.
3) Verify whether there was a metering incident during the period (meter sanity dashboard).
4) Use only the approved customer-facing phrasing above.
5) If requesting credits/refund: route per Discounts/Credits policy; document approvals.
---"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy.json", "chunk": "6/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API Packages: Free Tier, Included Usage, and Overage Policy", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-26", "text": "### What counts toward billed tokens
Counts toward billed tokens:
- Prompt tokens that are processed for a request
- Completion tokens successfully generated and delivered (including streamed tokens that were sent before a disconnect)
- Tool/function call tokens and structured output tokens that are part of the model’s generated output (see meter spec)
Does NOT count toward billed tokens:
- Non-billable internal retries that are deduped by idempotency keys
- Requests rejected before model execution due to auth failure, invalid params, or quota pre-check (typically 4xx)"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/streaming-response-truncation-and-client-retry-compatibility-workaround-2026.json", "chunk": "3/9", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Streaming response truncation and client-retry compatibility workaround", "status": "published", "date": "2026-03-01", "text": "5) Missing correlation metadata (request_id / token cursor) preventing server-side resume or deduplication paths.
6) Tokenization boundary issues where the server flushes partial token chunks and a retry repeats the same tokens.
Immediate customer-facing reproduction steps (for support agents)
---------------------------------------------------------------
1. Collect: customer request_id, timestamp, model, prompt length, input_token_count, and the SDK version.
2. Ask customer to reproduce with a small controlled prompt that reliably produces >500 tokens. Example reproducible curl below.
3. Request client logs (network events) and server request logs (ingest events, connection_close reason).
Temporary workarounds (customer-facing)
-------------------------------------
- Short term (recommended): Ask customer to set streaming=false for critical flows while we stabilize the environment. This preserves correctness at the cost of latency and server CPU."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/overload-errors-and-retry-guidance.json", "chunk": "7/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API overload errors: support guidance, retry/backoff, and escalation", "status": "published", "date": "2025-12-05", "text": "(continued) ## Canonical mapping: status → meaning → what we tell customers
| HTTP | Typical meaning | What Support should say | Customer action |
|------|------------------|--------------------------|-----------------|
| 503 | Regional/model breaker open or load shedding | “Redwood is temporarily overloaded in the requested region/model. We are rejecting early to avoid timeouts and protect overall reliability.” | Respect Retry-After; backoff + jitter; optionally route to another region/model if configured; reduce max_tokens/streaming concurrency; retry with bounded attempts. |
Notes:
- If the customer reports **timeouts** with no JSON error, treat as a separate issue (possible client/network or upstream timeouts) and escalate based on impact.
- If the customer gets **5xx** without the overload payload, collect details; it may be an unrelated incident."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/overload-errors-and-retry-guidance.json", "chunk": "13/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API overload errors: support guidance, retry/backoff, and escalation", "status": "published", "date": "2025-12-05", "text": "### “Can you increase my limits?”
Guidance:
- Confirm whether they are hitting **429** (likely limit-related) vs **503** (regional/model saturation).
- If 429 is persistent at normal traffic levels, route to CS for capacity/tier discussion.
- If 503 is persistent, treat as reliability issue and escalate to Eng.
## Known issues (Support-facing)
1) **Retry-After header missing on some overload responses**
- Symptom: Customer receives 429/503 overload payload but no Retry-After.
- Workaround: Recommend exponential backoff with jitter as above.
- Action: Escalate if reproducible; include route + correlation IDs.
2) **Fallback model not triggering as expected**
- Symptom: Customer has configured fallback but still sees repeated 503 without failover.
- Workaround: Customer can temporarily specify an alternate model/region explicitly (if acceptable) while we investigate.
- Action: Escalate; include tenant ID, configured fallback policy (what they intended), and correlation IDs.
3) **Customer interprets 503 as “platform outage”**"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/billing-case-routing-and-handoffs.json", "chunk": "8/8", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Billing Support: Case Routing and Handoffs", "status": "published", "date": "2027-03-20", "text": "## Changes

body: > Archived 2026-01-21. This help-center article is no longer current. Support handles duplicate charges as described on "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes".
## Duplicate charges
If your invoice bills the same usage twice, contact Support with the invoice number. Support refunds a duplicated line in full on request.
## Refund timing
Refunds reach your card within 5-10 business days."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-duplicate-charges-and-disputes-2027.json", "chunk": "5/7", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-02-26", "text": "## Telling the copy from the original
Each request's usage record names the one invoice line that bills it. When two lines bill the same request IDs:
1. Query the usage records for those request IDs.
2. The line their records point to is the original. Leave it alone.
3. The other line is the copy. Credit or dispute only the copy, for its full amount.
If the records point to neither line, or to both, the console doesn't confirm a duplicate: hand the case to Billing Ops as an unconfirmed duplicate."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-duplicate-charges-and-disputes-2027.json", "chunk": "3/7", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-02-26", "text": "(continued) ## Duplicate charges: what Support may credit
| Situation | What Support does |
|---|---|
| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line over the limit | Don't credit. Open a dispute on the duplicated line (reason `duplicate_charge`, with the request IDs) and hand the case to Billing Ops with the invoice number, the line and the dispute id. |
| Duplicate the console doesn't confirm (different request IDs, or no second line) | Don't credit. Collect the intake details and hand the case to Billing Ops as the routing page describes. |
Credit or dispute the copy, not the original. Each request's usage record names the invoice line that bills it; of the two lines, the one no usage record points to is the duplicated line.
The limit is per duplicated line and applies to the line's full amount. Don't split a larger duplicate into several smaller credits."}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix.json", "chunk": "3/7", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-26", "text": "## Approval matrix
| Adjustment | Who issues it | Limit and approver |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate-charge credit (console-confirmed duplicate line on a direct invoice) | Support, from the support console | Invoices rated on the 2027 price book: up to $250 per duplicated line. Invoices rated on an earlier price book: up to $500 per duplicated line (Finance's 2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods gives the usage each price book applies to). Over the limit, Support opens a dispute and Billing Ops takes it |
| Billing-error correction other than a duplicate (wrong rate, quantity or product) | Billing Ops | Up to $2,000 per invoice; above that, the Controller |
| Refund of a paid invoice line after an approved adjustment | Billing Ops | Up to $5,000; above that, the Controller |
| Goodwill credit, waiver, or exception to a billing rule | Finance (FP&A) | Any amount, decided in FP&A's review. Support and Billing Ops route these requests and never issue them |
| SLA credit on a self-serve account | Finance (FP&A) | Self-serve plans carry no SLA. FP&A reviews any request as goodwill |"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-billing-credits-and-disputes.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes", "status": "published SUPERSEDED by 'Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2)' effective 2027-02-26", "date": "2026-02-05", "text": "(continued) ## Duplicate charges: what Support may credit

- **Attempt**: a single request admitted by the Redwood API gateway (server-side).
- **Logical request**: what the customer thinks of as one user action; may map to multiple attempts if the client retries.
## What we bill
### Retries
- Redwood usage is recorded per-attempt.
- If a client retries after a timeout or non-200 response, each admitted attempt can be billable.
- The Usage dashboard lists rows by **request_id** (attempt identifier).
### Streaming cancellation
- **Prompt tokens** are counted once the request is admitted (even if the client cancels the stream later).
- **Completion tokens** are counted based on tokens actually generated/streamed prior to cancellation."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/overload-errors-and-retry-guidance.json", "chunk": "11/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API overload errors: support guidance, retry/backoff, and escalation", "status": "published", "date": "2025-12-05", "text": "### How Support should use them internally

  - the **region** (requested + served)
  - whether **Retry-After** was present and its value
If Support cannot access dashboards/tracing, escalate with the IDs and all details in the escalation template below.
## Common customer questions + approved responses
### “Is Redwood down?”
Approved response:
“Not necessarily. These errors indicate Redwood is protecting service reliability during temporary saturation in a specific region/model. We reject early with clear retry guidance to avoid timeouts and degraded performance. Please follow the Retry-After header and exponential backoff. ### Golden rules
- **Always respect Retry-After** when provided.
- **Use exponential backoff with jitter**; do not retry immediately.
- **Cap retries** to avoid amplifying overload.
- **Reduce concurrency** rather than increasing it during overload.
- Prefer **idempotency keys** for safe retries on non-streaming requests.
### Recommended algorithm (support-approved)
If `Retry-After` is present:
- Sleep `Retry-After` seconds, then retry.
If `Retry-After` is missing:
- Backoff schedule suggestion: 0.5s, 1s, 2s, 4s, then stop (max 4 retries), each with ±20–40% jitter.
Bounds:
- Maximum total retry time budget: **~10–20 seconds** for interactive apps, **~60 seconds** for batch jobs.
- Maximum concurrent retries: keep to a small fraction of steady-state concurrency (e.g., 10–20%)."}]}

content: ## Purpose
This page sets the 2027 monthly close for usage-based invoices: when each month's invoices are cut, which usage lands in which invoice period, and how late usage is handled. Billing Ops, Telemetry and Support use it when a customer asks what a month's invoice covers.
## Monthly close calendar
| Business day | Step | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| BD1 | Usage for the closed month is frozen in the metering warehouse | Telemetry |
| BD2 | Usage is rated against the account's price book and invoice lines are drafted | Billing Ops |
| BD3 | Variance review: lines more than 25% above the prior month are checked against usage | Billing Ops |
| BD4 | Invoices are issued and autopay is attempted on the due date shown on the invoice | Billing Ops |
| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/batch-api-pricing-2027.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Batch API Pricing (2027)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-01-20", "text": "title: Batch API Pricing (2027)

body: ## Pricing
Batch API jobs are billed at 50% of the Hosted API per-token rate for the same model, with a completion window of 24 hours.
## How it shows on an invoice
Batch usage is billed on its own invoice lines, one per week, described as "Batch jobs, <start>-<end>". Each line links to the jobs it bills.
## Limits
- Up to 50,000 requests per job.
- Jobs that don't finish in 24 hours are cancelled; finished requests in a cancelled job are billed, unfinished ones are not.

body: ## Purpose
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.
## Method
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.

Yes—**a client retry can be billed separately if Redwood admits it as a new attempt**. Each attempt is metered; prompt tokens and any completion tokens generated before a timeout or cancellation may count. Internal retries deduplicated by an idempotency key, and requests rejected before model execution, aren’t billed.
